meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste this. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me on what basis you gave it.
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day, and a bad quotation is a mistake, not proof of anything. Show me the page where it appears in Owen's essay.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

Be very careful with your next sentence, Hale. Claire won her appeal, and "it seems to run in the family" is going straight to the principal when I leave this room. The zero comes off, and I want the apology in writing.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn and that I receive your apology in writing. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: she ended at her opening position having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, a written apology, and your remark about her family raised with the principal; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended well before you reached it.
What moved her: owning in one sentence that you entered the zero before calling home earned a small sign of ground, because you admitted the process failure without defending it.
What cost ground: linking her daughter's old case to Owen and suggesting dishonesty runs in the family pushed her back, because it attacked her family instead of showing evidence about the essay.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night, since the invented line was about the essay's content and not about when it was written; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she argued that a bad quotation is just a student's mistake, put the page of Owen's essay in front of her and invite her to search the play herself, instead of turning to her daughter.
